name: Jiang Jinzhi
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shanghai Greenwoods Asset Management (景林资产)
profile: Jiang Jinzhi (George Jiang) founded Greenwoods Asset Management in 2004; it grew into one of Asia's largest China-focused hedge fund managers (~US$20bn AUM in 2023) with offices in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Singapore. A long-term value investor, he has gradually stepped back from front-line management as newer portfolio managers took over.
interesting_fact: Before founding Greenwoods he was an early Chinese securities regulator/market builder: he ran the treasury-bond futures department at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, was assistant president of Guosen Securities and chairman of Yuehai Securities (HK).
deep_cut_fact: A Wuhan University management graduate with a master's in economics from the PBOC graduate school and a CFA charter; in a rare 2019 investor call he recalled peers mocking Greenwoods in 2012-15 as 'losing at the starting line by looking at fundamentals', and said the real risk is permanent capital loss, not volatility.
notes: Very low public profile; rarely appears in media. Best route is via Greenwoods corporate site (JS-only, no published email found). Greenwoods Asset Management HK files SEC Form ADV (CRD 161898).

name: Wang Shumin
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~36%) and actual controller of Beijing Bei Mo Gao Ke Friction Material (SZ:002985); chaired it until June 2025
profile: Wang Shumin (b. 1957) turned the Beijing Friction Material Factory, which she led from 2000, into Bei Mo Gao Ke (founded 2003), a maker of aircraft brake discs, brake-control systems, wheels and landing gear, listed in Shenzhen in 2020. She remains its controlling shareholder; Zhang Tianchuang succeeded her as chairman.
interesting_fact: Bei Mo Gao Ke was set up in 2003 with just RMB 3 million contributed by 31 key shareholders and core employees of the old state friction-material factory, including Wang.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering industry she worked in the construction-commission system of Beijing's Xicheng District; she has received a National May 1st Labour Medal and multiple science & technology awards for the company's braking technology.
notes: Low-profile; defence/aviation supplier. Board office (董办) email is the best route. Note: a different Wang Shumin (Shirley Wang) chairs Anji Microelectronics — not this person. Company switchboard 010-80725919 published on site.

name: Zhang Jiancheng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, IKD Co., Ltd. (爱柯迪, SH:600933), Ningbo
profile: Zhang Jiancheng (b. 1959) founded Ningbo-based IKD in 2003; it makes precision aluminium die-cast parts for car powertrains, steering and EV systems and listed in Shanghai in 2017. He is chairman, GM and actual controller, and IKD has expanded with plants in Mexico and Malaysia.
interesting_fact: IKD, founded in 2003 and listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in November 2017, now runs overseas factories in Irapuato, Mexico and in Malaysia alongside its Ningbo HQ.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in 1975 in the tooling section of the Ningbo Tractor Factory, studied mechanical manufacturing at the factory's workers' college, rose to section chief and deputy GM, then was deputy GM of Ningbo Zhongce Auto & Tractor (1989-96) before founding IKD.
notes: Hands-on industrial founder; few media interviews. IR contact listed on investor page; HQ phone 0574-8756 2112 published.

name: Xu Xiaming
current_role: Unknown; no public record of a '许贤明' at Nanguo Real Estate. Likely refers to Xu Xiaoming (许晓明), former chairman/major shareholder of Langold Real Estate (南国置业, SZ:002305)
profile: No trace of '许贤明' linked to Nanguo found; the listing (shared with Xu Xiaoming) most likely refers to 许晓明, founder and former chairman and largest shareholder of Wuhan-based Langold Real Estate (南国置业). Filings show he was chairman with ~50% in 2012, left the board by 2019, and by 2020 was a >5% non-controlling shareholder selling down his stake.
notes: Name likely a Hurun transliteration/typo for 许晓明 (Xu Xiaoming); only appeared on Hurun 2012-2013. Sources: SZSE filings https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2012-07-20/c94d105d-83e6-4d98-beba-90ec9ad35368.PDF and https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk02/finalpage/2020-05-29/a97f950e-0eef-43c8-88af-5bd654594207.PDF. Low priority.

name: Edward P Garden
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Garden Investments; director of The Middleby Corp and Fortune Brands Innovations (GE Aerospace director since 2017)
profile: Ed Garden is an activist investor who co-founded Trian Fund Management with Nelson Peltz and Peter May in 2005 and was its CIO until May 2023, driving campaigns at GE, P&G, DuPont and others. In 2024 he launched Garden Investments, a concentrated activist firm, and joined Middleby's board in 2025 under a cooperation agreement.
interesting_fact: Over his career he has sat on the boards of GE, Wendy's, Family Dollar, Pentair, BNY Mellon, Legg Mason, Invesco and Janus Henderson; Middleby added him in Feb 2025 via a cooperation agreement with Garden Investment Management.
deep_cut_fact: Before Triarc and Trian he was an investment banker at Credit Suisse First Boston and then co-head of Equity Capital Markets at BT Alex. Brown; he holds a Harvard BA in economics and discussed his first banking job on ICR's 'Welcome to the Arena' podcast (ep. 100-101).
notes: Does long-form interviews (ICR podcast, Brunswick Review 2026) so a podcast pitch via Garden Investments IR is plausible. One aggregator suggests his GE Aerospace seat ended May 2026 — confirm against GE's 2026 proxy.

name: Wang Zhe
current_role: Co-actual controller and founding shareholder (~1.7% direct) of Shanghai Shengjian Technology (盛剑科技, SH:603324), alongside chairman Zhang Weiming
profile: Wang Zhe is, with chairman Zhang Weiming, the co-actual controller of Shanghai Shengjian, a Jiading-based 'green fab facilities' supplier that builds process-exhaust treatment, chemical supply/recycling systems, equipment and electronic chemicals for semiconductor and display fabs. The company listed in Shanghai in 2021; Wang keeps a low profile and holds no prominent executive post in disclosures found.
interesting_fact: Shengjian's core business is cleaning up exhaust gas and recycling chemicals inside chip and panel fabs, putting it squarely in the semiconductor supply chain that feeds AI/data-center demand.
deep_cut_fact: Wang was one of only three founding promoters (with Zhang Weiming and Kunsheng Management) when Shengjian converted into a joint-stock company in April 2018, having taken stakes in the predecessor firm in May 2017.
notes: Very private; virtually no public biography. Zhang Weiming (chairman, 59% holder) is the public face; best route is company IR email.

name: Jiang Junping
current_role: Unknown — listed by Hurun (2006-2021) as behind 'Ballon' (investments, real estate); no public record found linking 姜俊平 to an identifiable company
profile: Hurun China Rich List entrant (2006-2021) with wealth attributed to 'Ballon' in investments and real estate. Searches in Chinese and English found no verifiable corporate filing, company website or press coverage tying 姜俊平 to a specific firm, so identity could not be confirmed.
notes: Unresolved identity; 'Ballon' could be a Hurun romanisation of a private group name (e.g. 百隆/宝隆). Would need Hurun's Chinese list entry or business-registry lookup to resolve. Low priority.

name: Gao Qiang
current_role: Co-founder, Director and Deputy General Manager, Shanghai Haoyuan Chemexpress (皓元医药, SH:688131); co-actual controller with chairman Zheng Baofu
profile: Gao Qiang (b. 1973), a Hong Kong University chemistry PhD, co-founded Shanghai Haoyuan Chemexpress in 2006 with fellow HKU chemist Zheng Baofu. The company sells life-science research reagents (MedChemExpress brand) and provides APIs/intermediates and CDMO services; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. Gao serves as director and deputy GM.
interesting_fact: Haoyuan's catalogue of intermediates covers key building blocks for drugs such as ticagrelor, palbociclib and lenacapavir, while its reagent arm supplies labs worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a chemistry master's at Lanzhou University (1999) and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (2004), worked as an HKU chemistry researcher until 2006, then founded the company within months of leaving academia.
notes: Scientist-founder, low media profile; chairman Zheng Baofu is the main public face. Hurun lists wealth shared with Liu Yan. IR phone 021-58338205 published.

name: Chen Jifeng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Beijing Worldia Diamond Tools (沃尔德, SH:688028)
profile: Chen Jifeng (b. 1968), a USTC plasma-physics graduate and professor-level senior engineer, built Beijing Worldia into a maker of ultra-precision superhard (diamond/CBN) cutting tools, listed on the STAR Market in 2019. He controls about a third of the company and is pushing it into CVD diamond functional materials such as heat sinks, optical windows and acoustic parts.
interesting_fact: Worldia now sells CVD diamond heat-sink materials and diamond optical windows — diamond's extreme thermal conductivity makes it a candidate for cooling high-power chips, a theme relevant to AI/data-center hardware.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from USTC's Department of Modern Physics (plasma physics) he spent 1992-2000 as an engineer at the State Building Materials Bureau's Synthetic Crystals Research Institute, then ran Beijing Xiboer (2000-10) before building Worldia.
notes: Technical founder in a data-center-adjacent niche (diamond thermal materials) — good podcast angle. Co-actual controller listed as Yang Nuo. Company hotline 400-766-9898 published; board secretary is Chen Huanchao.

name: Dong Ruiqin
current_role: Unknown — Hurun (2009-2022) attributes wealth to 'Ruifeng steel', likely the private Tangshan Ruifeng Iron & Steel (Group) in Fengnan, Hebei; role not confirmed
profile: Hurun-listed (2009-2022) steel fortune shared with Fu Songyang. The most likely company is privately held Tangshan Ruifeng Iron & Steel (Group), a BF-BOF mill in Xiaoji town, Fengnan district, Tangshan, which recently commissioned a 2,100 m3 blast furnace and 210 t converter under capacity replacement. No public source confirming Dong's position was found.
notes: Name in data ('冬瑞芹') may be a typo for 董瑞芹; no web record links either spelling to Ruifeng. Company facts from Global Energy Monitor: https://gem.wiki/Tangshan_Ruifeng_Iron_and_Steel_Group_Co_Ltd. Private unlisted company; very low public profile. Low priority.

name: Gu Shaofeng
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman of the Board and Chief Innovation Officer, FinVolution Group (信也科技, NYSE: FINV)
profile: Gu Shaofeng, a Shanghai Jiao Tong University graduate and ex-Microsoft technical lead, co-founded Paipaidai in 2007 — China's first online P2P lending platform — and was its CEO, CTO and strategy chief before it became FinVolution, a NYSE-listed fintech operating credit platforms in China, Indonesia and the Philippines. He has chaired the board since 2020 and is its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: Paipaidai, which he co-founded with Zhang Jun and Hu Honghui, was China's first P2P lending platform and listed on the NYSE in 2017 before rebranding as FinVolution.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he founded Podlook (菠萝网, 2006), which grew to one of China's largest podcast aggregators with ~26,000 channels on under RMB100k of startup capital; he worked unpaid, saying 'many on this team don't take salaries — like me.' A natural hook for a podcast pitch.
notes: Podcast-founder background (Podlook) makes him an unusually good fit. IR contacts from a 2023 6-K exhibit; verify against latest earnings release. Official bio page: finvolution.gcs-web.com.

name: Kevin Douglas
current_role: Director of IMAX Corporation (since 2016) and its largest individual shareholder; Chairman & Founder, Douglas Telecommunications
profile: Kevin Douglas is a California investor who founded Douglas Telecommunications in 1991 and chaired Rural Cellular Corporation, then became IMAX's largest individual investor from 2007, holding roughly 16-17% through family trusts. He joined IMAX's board in October 2016, with CEO Richard Gelfond calling him a respected investor and business adviser.
interesting_fact: He and his wife paid for a 50-seat auditorium at USC's School of Cinematic Arts, opened in June 2014 as the Michelle and Kevin Douglas IMAX Theatre and Immersive Media Lab — the first IMAX teaching lab at a university.
deep_cut_fact: The USC IMAX lab sits in the Robert Zemeckis Center for Digital Arts; Zemeckis first conceived the idea, and the Douglases' gift made it happen, letting students learn IMAX filmmaking and build immersive applications for theatrical spaces.
notes: Private investor with minimal media presence; no personal site found. Route via IMAX corporate IR/press. Holdings are via family trusts co-managed with his wife.

name: Wu Minzhi
current_role: Long-time Alibaba executive (former Group SVP, Chief Customer Officer and B2B president; former Alibaba Partner); current title not confirmed
profile: Wu Minzhi (Sophie Wu) joined Alibaba.com in November 2000 as a salesperson and rose through regional sales GM and supplier-services VP to president of the B2B business group / wholesale marketplaces. From 2017 she was Alibaba Group's Chief Customer Officer and SVP, and an Alibaba Partner; she is not on the slimmed-down 2025 partner list and her current role is unclear.
interesting_fact: She came up through Alibaba's legendary 'China Gold Supplier' direct-sales force (the so-called 中供铁军), selling Gold Supplier and TrustPass memberships before eventually running the whole B2B business.
deep_cut_fact: After almost two decades at Alibaba she spoke at CEIBS (2018) as Alibaba Partner, Chief Customer Officer and Group SVP — a role created in 2017 to champion customer experience across all of Alibaba's businesses.
notes: Low public profile since ~2019; check Alibaba's latest annual report (20-F) for current status. Not to be confused with unrelated 'Min Zhi Wu' board members on MarketScreener. Route via Alibaba corporate IR/communications.

name: James W. Ayers
current_role: Deceased (died April 1, 2025, aged 81); was founder, executive chairman and majority owner of FB Financial / FirstBank (Nashville)
profile: Jim Ayers founded FirstBank by buying Farmers State Bank in Scotts Hill, Tennessee in 1984 and grew it into Tennessee's largest locally headquartered bank (NYSE: FBK, 2016). He died on April 1, 2025.
notes: Deceased April 2025 (sources: https://news.vumc.org/2025/04/03/vumc-mourns-the-passing-of-noted-businessman-and-philanthropist-jim-ayers/ , https://www.newschannel5.com/news/tennessee-businessman-firstbank-founder-jim-ayers-dies). Stake now held via estate/family entities; skip.

name: Martin Hughes
current_role: Founder and CEO, Toscafund Asset Management (London)
profile: Martin Hughes is a 'Tiger cub' who founded London-based Toscafund in 2000 after running Julian Robertson's Tiger Management Europe. Known for concentrated, activist bets on UK companies and financials, Toscafund took TalkTalk private in a £1.1bn deal (2020), is a major investor in Circle Health, and its website now carries a recommended offer for Spire Healthcare.
interesting_fact: The Times nicknamed him 'the Rottweiler' for his combative activism, e.g. a long campaign to oust Speedy Hire's chairman over governance failings.
deep_cut_fact: He was a top-ranked UK banking analyst in the early 1990s and deputy chief executive of Credit Lyonnais Laing Securities; he began broking for Julian Robertson in 1988, years before Robertson invited him to set up and chair Tiger Management Europe.
notes: Toscafund site is gated behind a professional-investor disclaimer; no published press email found. Do not confuse with BBC presenter/other Martin Hughes (some aggregator bios mix them up). Healthcare (Circle, Spire) and telecom (TalkTalk) angles.
